title: My Entire Home Espresso Setup (After 3 Years of Upgrades)
creator: Theo Marsh
description:
Three years, way too many grinders, and this is where I landed.

GEAR IN THIS VIDEO (affiliate links, I earn a small commission if you buy through them):
Grinder: Niche Zero - https://amzn.to/3xQ7kLp
Machine: Lelit Bianca - https://amzn.to/4bR2mNs
Scale: Acaia Lunar - https://amzn.to/3VdTq0w
Tamper + knock box: https://amzn.to/3Kp9wXe

I bought everything here myself. Nothing in this video was sent to me.

Instagram: @theomarshcoffee

sentences.t: Okay, so a lot of you have asked what's actually on my counter these days.
And honestly it's changed so much since the last setup video that I figured it was time.
This is three years of buying things, selling things, and regretting things.
Let's start with the grinder, because that's the one that actually matters.
This is the Niche Zero.
I know, I know, everyone has one, it's basically the default now.
But there's a reason for that.
It's single dose, so I weigh out eighteen grams, drop it in, and there's almost nothing left behind in the burrs.
Before this I had a big flat burr grinder that held like four grams of stale coffee in it at all times, which, yeah, not great.
The one thing I don't love is the noise, it's kind of a low growl, and my partner has opinions about it at six in the morning.
Okay, the machine.
This is the Lelit Bianca, and this is where I went a little overboard.
It's dual boiler, so I can steam milk and pull a shot at the same time.
And it's got this wooden paddle on top that lets you control the flow while the shot's running.
Do you need flow control?
No, absolutely not.
Is it fun to mess with on a Sunday morning?
Very much yes.
I'll be honest, for the first two months I was making worse coffee with it than with my old single boiler, because I kept fiddling.
Once I stopped touching the paddle and just let it do a slow pre-infusion, it got really, really good.
Now the small stuff, which people always underestimate.
The scale is an Acaia Lunar.
It's tiny, it fits right on the drip tray, and it starts the timer by itself when the first drop hits.
The tamper is just a calibrated one I got for like thirty bucks, nothing fancy.
Knock box, same deal, it's a box, you knock things into it.
And I've got a little WDT tool, which is basically a bunch of acupuncture needles stuck in a cork.
Sounds ridiculous, but it breaks up the clumps and my shots stopped channeling almost overnight.
Oh, and real quick, before I forget.
Everything I've shown you is linked down in the description, mostly on Amazon.
Those are affiliate links, so if you pick something up through them I get a small commission, and it doesn't cost you anything extra.
I bought all of this myself, nobody sent me any of it, so it's just the stuff I actually use every day.
But if you were going to buy a grinder anyway, going through the link does help the channel out a little bit.
Okay, so what would I buy again if I was starting over?
Honestly, the grinder, a hundred percent, day one.
If you've got a limited budget, put most of it into the grinder and get a cheaper machine.
A great grinder with a basic machine beats a fancy machine with a bad grinder every single time.
The Bianca I'd probably skip, if I'm being honest with myself.
It's amazing, but something simpler would get me ninety percent of the way there for half the price.
The scale I'd buy again, the WDT tool I'd buy again, it costs about five dollars.
And the one thing I wish I'd bought way earlier is a decent water filter, because my tap water was scaling up the old machine like crazy.
That's a whole separate video though.
Alright, let me pull one shot so you can see the whole flow.
Eighteen in, timer on, and we're looking for about thirty-six out in around thirty seconds.
There it goes, look at that color.
That's the good stuff.
If you've got questions about any of this, leave them in the comments, I do read them.
Thanks for hanging out, and I'll see you next week.
